tool_analysis:
Step Analysis: The recorded browser session demonstrates navigating to the Magento admin Shipments grid, using column-level filters (Shipment #, Order #, Ship to Name, Date and Qty ranges), applying Search, using Select Visible, running mass actions (PDF Packingslips and Print Shipping Labels), exporting results (CSV observed; Excel attempted), and opening individual shipment View pages. Stable selectors were identified by anchoring to column header text and by URL patterns for per-row View links.

Task Definition: Create a reusable tool that: (1) navigates to the admin shipments grid, (2) applies provided filters, (3) triggers Search, (4) optionally selects visible rows, (5) optionally sets and submits a mass-action, (6) optionally selects an export format and triggers Export, and (7) optionally opens a shipment View page and extracts shipment-level details. The tool assumes the admin session is already authenticated (no login steps included).

Action Plan:
- Navigate to the shipments list (URL constructed from admin_url). Wait for the page to load.
- Input each filter value using XPath selectors anchored to header text (deterministic and stable across themes/locales where header text remains). This avoids brittle DOM indices.
- Click the Search button and wait for grid refresh.
- Extract the filtered results (rows and messages) for downstream use.
- Click Select Visible to select visible rows, then set the mass-action select to the provided option value and click Submit to execute the bulk action. Wait for completion and capture messages.
- Choose an export format (CSV/Excel/XML) from the Export control and click Export to trigger download. Wait briefly for the action.
- If a shipment id is provided, navigate to the shipment View URL and extract shipment-level controls and data.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- admin_url: required (base admin URL). Used for navigation and building shipment view URL.
- shipment_number, order_number, ship_to_name, total_qty_from, total_qty_to, date_shipped_from, date_shipped_to, order_date_from, order_date_to: optional filter inputs.
- export_format: optional export format (CSV/Excel/XML).
- mass_action_value: optional mass action option value (use actual select option values such as 'pdfshipments_order' or 'print_shipping_label').
- select_visible: optional boolean to attempt selecting visible rows prior to mass action.
- submit_mass_action: optional boolean to indicate intent to submit after selecting mass action (the tool will attempt the submit step regardless; set true to indicate you expect submission).
- view_shipment_id: optional shipment internal id to open the shipment view page for inspection.

Step Optimization: All UI interactions were replaced with stable XPath-based selectors anchored to visible label text or URL patterns where possible. Navigation to the main shipments list is performed directly via URL instead of clicking menus. Export and mass-action controls are targeted relative to their labels (e.g., 'Export to', 'Actions') rather than brittle DOM indices. Where the recorded session provided elementHash values, I preferred XPath label-relative selectors to increase robustness across environments. The tool contains no conditional branching; optional inputs may be passed as empty values to be effectively no-ops. The tool focuses only on essential interactions required by the original task.
name: magento_admin_shipments_tool
description: Filter and act on Magento 1.x admin Shipments grid: apply filters (Shipment #, Order #, Ship to Name, Date/Qty ranges), run grid Search/Reset, perform exports (CSV/Excel/XML), run mass-actions (PDF Packingslips, Print Shipping Labels) and open shipment View pages. The tool assumes an active admin session and an admin base URL is provided.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento admin Shipments grid (starting point for filters, exports and mass actions).
Wait for the shipments page to load and grid to render.
Enter the Shipment # filter value under the Shipment # column filter (leave blank to not filter by shipment number).
Enter the Order # filter value under the Order # column filter (leave blank to not filter by order number).
Enter the Ship to Name filter value below the Ship to Name column header (leave blank to not filter by name).
Enter the Total Qty 'From' filter (leave blank to skip).
Enter the Total Qty 'To' filter (leave blank to skip).
Enter Date Shipped 'From' (format MM/DD/YYYY). Leave blank to skip.
Enter Date Shipped 'To' (format MM/DD/YYYY). Leave blank to skip.
Enter Order Date 'From' (format MM/DD/YYYY). Leave blank to skip.
Enter Order Date 'To' (format MM/DD/YYYY). Leave blank to skip.
Click the Search button to apply the grid filters.
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying filters.
Capture the list of shipments currently visible and any success/error/notice messages.
steps.goal: Extract filtered grid rows (shipment increment id, order increment id, ship to name, total qty, view link) and page messages

steps.description: Click 'Select Visible' to select all visible rows (this is safe if there are no visible rows).
Set the mass-action select to the provided mass action option value (e.g. 'pdfshipments_order' or 'print_shipping_label'). Leave empty to keep default/no action.
Click the mass-action Submit to execute the selected mass action (if any).
Wait for the mass-action to process (watch for AJAX loaders and messages).
Choose an export format from the 'Export to' control (CSV/Excel/XML). Leave empty to skip export.
Click the Export button to trigger the export in the selected format.
Wait briefly for the export request or download to initiate.
Open a specific shipment's View page if view_shipment_id is provided (navigate to shipment details).
Wait for the shipment view page to load.
Capture shipment-level controls and data for verification or further automation.
steps.goal: Extract shipment view controls and details (Print, Create Shipping Label, carrier select, tracking number field, shipment items and history)

input_schema.name: admin_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL including /admin path, e.g. 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin'

input_schema.name: shipment_number
input_schema.description: Shipment increment id to filter by (exact text match). Example: '100000032'

input_schema.name: order_number
input_schema.description: Order increment id to filter by (exact text match). Example: '100000199'

input_schema.name: ship_to_name
input_schema.description: Ship to Name text to filter by (partial or full). Example: 'Jane Smith'

input_schema.name: total_qty_from
input_schema.description: Minimum Total Qty filter (numeric). Leave empty to skip. Example: '1'

input_schema.name: total_qty_to
input_schema.description: Maximum Total Qty filter (numeric). Leave empty to skip. Example: '10'

input_schema.name: date_shipped_from
input_schema.description: Date Shipped 'From' value (MM/DD/YYYY). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: date_shipped_to
input_schema.description: Date Shipped 'To' value (MM/DD/YYYY). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: order_date_from
input_schema.description: Order Date 'From' value (MM/DD/YYYY). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: order_date_to
input_schema.description: Order Date 'To' value (MM/DD/YYYY). Leave empty to skip.

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Export format to choose in the 'Export to' control. Use 'CSV', 'Excel' or 'XML'. Leave empty to skip export.

input_schema.name: mass_action_value
input_schema.description: Mass-action option value to select (use actual option value). Common values observed: 'pdfshipments_order' (PDF Packingslips), 'print_shipping_label' (Print Shipping Labels). Leave empty to skip mass action.

input_schema.name: select_visible
input_schema.description: If true, click 'Select Visible' before performing mass action. If false or omitted, selection step will still be attempted but can be a no-op.

input_schema.name: submit_mass_action
input_schema.description: If true, click the mass-action Submit after selecting the mass action. If false, the tool will still set the mass-action select (no guaranteed submit).

input_schema.name: view_shipment_id
input_schema.description: Internal shipment id to open the shipment View page (numeric id from URL). Example: '35' to open /sales_shipment/view/shipment_id/35/
